issues.description: Breaking rename of public frame class without deprecation alias
issues.detail: RequestMetadataFrame was an exported symbol in pipecat.frames.frames. Renaming it outright with no deprecation alias (e.g., RequestMetadataFrame = ServiceSwitcherRequestMetadataFrame) will break any external subclass or import. The changelog is marked 'changed' but downstream users importing the old name get an ImportError with no warning path.

issues.description: Forward reference to FrameProcessor risks runtime/circular issues
issues.detail: The new field is typed as `service: "FrameProcessor"` but there is no import of FrameProcessor in frames.py (even under TYPE_CHECKING). If dataclass field introspection or any tooling calls get_type_hints(), it will fail to resolve. Also worth confirming there is no circular import problem motivating the string annotation; if so, document why.

issues.description: Service identity comparison uses == instead of `is`
issues.detail: In push_frame, `frame.service == self.strategy.active_service` compares FrameProcessor instances by equality. FrameProcessor likely doesn't override __eq__, so this falls back to identity, but if any subclass does (or later does) override equality, two distinct services could compare equal and the wrong frame would be consumed. Use `is` for identity comparison of processor instances.

issues.description: ServiceSwitcherRequestMetadataFrame from inactive service now leaks downstream
issues.detail: Previously all RequestMetadataFrame instances were suppressed by the switcher. Now only frames targeting the active service are consumed; if a frame targeting a non-active service ever reaches push_frame (e.g., during a rapid switch race), it now leaks downstream as an unhandled control frame. Consider always consuming the frame regardless of target, since it is described as internal to the switcher.

issues.description: Docstring/behavior mismatch: frame is no longer 'silently consumed' by services
issues.detail: STTService and the mock now push the frame downstream after handling, but the class docstring still describes it as 'internal to the switcher.' Downstream processors will now see this control frame; document expected handling (ignore is fine) and confirm no downstream processor in the codebase reacts to the old/new type incorrectly.

issues.description: Ordering change in STTService: metadata now pushed before the request frame
issues.detail: Previously _push_stt_metadata was called and the RequestMetadataFrame was dropped. Now metadata is pushed, then the request frame is pushed downstream. Downstream observers (loggers, tests, recorders) may now see a request frame after the metadata, which is a subtle behavioral change worth a test asserting ordering and that no consumer is surprised.

review.summary: The rename is mechanically clean and tests are updated, but a few concerns deserve attention before merge. The biggest is the unannounced breaking rename of a public frame class with no deprecation alias, which will silently break external importers. The new `service` field uses a string-quoted FrameProcessor without a TYPE_CHECKING import, and the identity check uses `==` rather than `is`, both of which are fragile. Finally, the semantic change from 'silently consumed' to 'pushed downstream after handling' alters observable behavior and the class docstring no longer matches the actual flow.
